text: At the shepherd's hut on the edge of the waste, Zura fulfills her vow to Corvel: Find a New Colony for the Settlement closes with a strong hit. She stands alone with the Hound, Eddar holding Holtfen behind her, the old settlement three days east.

At first light, Zura walks into the old Ashfen settlement with Grey and a pack of goat-meat. Reach Your Destination — strong hit. The people see her coming and read the answer in her walking. Corvel meets her at the gate; the settlement learns the ground has been found.

In plain sight, with Ashfen gathered around her, Zura speaks: 'It's time to leave this place and find a home in a new Understanding. This one has to be left behind. Tomorrow we head out. Take nothing that came from the earth here.' Then she sets the root-cellar alight. The settlement watches their winter burn. Saela recognizes the act for what it is — a clean transfer. Corvel does not interfere.

[Recovered from sixhat-1 backup — originally recorded 2026-04-27T11:48] Zura followed a contract trail to an unnamed Hinterlands settlement (later named Ashfen), two days southeast of Ashford. The settlement's fungal colony had died overnight six weeks prior, trapping all settlers in compulsive iron-memory circles. Grey scouted, refused to re-enter. Zura circled the perimeter, saw circling settlers and a watcher at the forge, swore a formidable vow to free the settlement. Inside the forge she found an iron map — a vow-conductor built by Eddar to contain the settlers. She burned the map; the circling stopped. Eddar revealed himself from the forge's dark corner — he'd been watching the whole time, saw her swear at the treeline. He claims to be an itinerant who built the map as containment, not cause, and was seeking a cure. He's telling partial truths. The settlers' fate — freed or killed — is still unknown. The conversation is mid-scene in the forge.

[Recovered from sixhat-1 backup — originally recorded 2026-04-27T21:07] Zura fulfilled her formidable vow to free the Ashfen settlement. She volunteered as the vow-receiver — taking the settlers' unfulfilled harvest debt into her own iron alongside Greyhollow's existing vow. Eddar mediated the transfer using the salvaged iron map. The settlers woke. Fen reunited with her family. Immediately after, Eddar revealed his true purpose: something answered the broken Ironbinder vow when Greyhollow fell and is still moving through dead colonies as doors. He needs Zura to lead him to Lago Rhian. The vow is closed (weak hit — 1 experience earned). Zura now carries two settlement harvest vows in her iron: Greyhollow's and Ashfen's.

[Recovered from sixhat-1 backup — originally recorded 2026-04-29T02:57 (session 2)] Miss on Undertake a Journey (Shadow). Twenty minutes into the treeline, Grey froze. The soil had gone Rot-grey — dead colony grey — ten minutes northeast of Ashfen, spreading through the old fungal network. Zura heard her father's voice through the dead colony conducting her Greyhollow harvest vow: her name, spoken as he said it when she was small. Eddar concluded someone connected to Greyhollow passed through recently — possibly Lago — though Zura noted this may be his obsession speaking. Zura paid the price: -2 spirit. Her resolve: "If we come across him, my vow is simply rushing to meet me." They pushed on once the grey soil ended.

[Recovered from sixhat-1 backup — originally recorded 2026-04-29T02:58 (session 2)] Miss on Reach Your Destination (progress score 4). Arrived at Holtfen to find it massively overcrowded — six to eight settlements' worth of displaced people in a space for one. Unsettling calm among the settlers (quieted by the living colony's iron). Dalla stood in the longhouse doorway watching the gate — she had positioned two people at exits. She recognized Zura's Greyhollow iron-marks immediately and was clearly expecting someone like her. First meeting: Dalla said "Greyhollow. You've been carrying that one a long time." Journey to Holtfen resolved; vow progress track retained at 4 boxes (the journey was real work toward the vow). Supply: 2. Spirit: 3.

[Recovered from sixhat-1 backup — originally recorded 2026-04-29T02:58 (session 3)] First longhouse meeting with Dalla and Eddar. Dalla revealed her plan: she has been gathering displaced settlers with live harvest vows from dead colonies to Holtfen for 8 months, using the living colony to keep them stable. She needs a vow-receiver to take all the aggregate vow-debt and formally transfer it into Holtfen's colony — closing the doors the Answering uses. She had been looking for someone like Zura specifically. Eddar and Dalla have prior history and tension: he hunts the source (Lago), she manages symptoms (closing vow-doors). Colony assessment: the tender confirmed Holtfen can take one more small settlement (Ashfen) — but no more after that. Sojourn strong hit: +2 spirit, +2 supply.

Day four of the march, mid-morning. Undertake a Journey: miss with match (4+1 vs 5,5). The oracle delivered Eliminate / Ruin. Arda — the old woman with the dry cough — falters on flat track. Her hands have gone fen-belt grey; skin crackles like lichen at the joints. She confesses: late-sworn harvest vow, never disclosed. The Answering is in her, reading her, and through her the rest of the column. Up and down the line, settlers check their own hands. Corvel understands the stakes instantly: if Arda is taken before they reach Holtfen, The Answering gets a thread into the whole transfer. He asks Zura what to do.

Day four, mid-morning. Zura cuts herself and Arda out of the column. Speaks to Corvel but for everyone: she and Arda cannot enter Holtfen as they are; the rest must go on. Arda names her daughter — Enya — one syllable pressed into her palm like a token. Enya vows to Zura, not her mother: "I will keep her hearth. At Holtfen." Zura witnesses it. Corvel leads the column east without a word; Fen takes her father's shoulder; Grey goes with her on Zura's word. Zura and Arda are left on the track with a cold wind and an unanswered question: where do two dead women go?

Night before Holtfen, Brennan's cottage. Zura knelt at the hearth and began to Swear an Iron Vow to remove Caldren as warden captain of Holtfen — expose, depose, drive out, or kill, one way or another. Miss (Heart 1 + 1 vs 9, 7). The obstacle surfaced immediately: Lona, awake at the door, stopped her. Caldren was her captain, not Zura's; an outsider accusing him gives him the easy out, but Holtfen will hear Lona. Zura pressed on by accepting Lona's terms — a joint vow. Suffered -2 momentum (M 3 → 1). Hadris left free to choose at the gate tomorrow. The vow is dangerous rank, Zura's on her sheet but bound to Lona's standing at resolution.

Dalla's longhouse, morning of the arrival. Zura walked in through the back with Lona and Hadris. Dalla, Esther (Saelin's mother, council seat held for her), Harel the smith, and Besren the old speaker were seated. Esther cried seeing Hadris alive — Caldren had told the council he was dead. Zura confirmed Ashfen had survived the aggregate transfer, Corvel forging for Harel, Fen sleeping three nights a week under Dalla's roof. Then Zura laid out the facts: seven First-Born stones bind things the settlement can't fight; Caldren's circuit used to tend them; six winters ago Caldren stopped tending and cut tags of wardens who tended on their own time (Lona, Hadris, Ewa); three men sent to kill Hadris at the birch stand; the cracked stone was deliberate neglect on a schedule; Maret tended the next-nearest with her grandmother's songs because the circuit hadn't come in a month; and the Bound Thing that rose from the cracked stone. Dalla: 'If what you've said is true, Caldren dies or leaves today. If what you've said is not true, you die or leave today.' Zura offered to Draw the Circle.

Draw the Circle — strong hit with a match (Heart 1+5 vs 3,3). At the well-ground in full view of Holtfen, Zura traced her half of the ring, then bared herself — stripped to a leather halter in freezing air, sword-tip driven into the earth, sending Grey to stay outside the line and calling Caldren over with a finger-curl. Term declared by Besren: 'to death's door' (surrender allowed, death not the named outcome). Boast declared at the ring: 'bare yourself' — his harm +1 against her. +1 momentum for the strong hit, +1 for the boast. Total M 3→5. Initiative to Zura.

Opening exchange of the duel. Zura opened with a feint-and-switch — lunge in right hand, sword changes to left hand mid-commit, tip inside Caldren's guard at his hip. Secure an Advantage +Shadow, miss with a match (Shadow 2+5 vs 8,8). The trick physically worked but *told* Caldren what she was — he recognized Mai's sword-line and countered with the hip-line guard only Mai teaches. He asked 'Who trained you, girl?' and took initiative with a Strike. Match-on-miss revelation: Caldren has been trained in Mai's line by someone. Someone who passed through this circuit eight winters ago.

Second exchange of the duel. Caldren Strike against Zura's bared right side; Zura chose Clash over Face Danger, stepped INTO his cut chest-to-chest, drove a short hip-powered cut up under his chestpiece. Clash strong hit with a match (Iron 3+6 vs 1,1). Chose Find an Opening (+1 harm) and burned momentum for Swordmaster's +2 harm bonus. 5 harm total = 10 progress boxes against a dangerous-rank foe = Caldren's combat track maxed in one blow. Caldren's wardens at the gate started to move; Harel raised the iron rod without looking and they stopped. Momentum burn: M 5→2 (reset).

End the Fight — strong hit (progress 10 vs 6,7). Zura pressed sword-point into Caldren's chest and walked him backward over his own half-line of the circle. He went out on his knees. Harel unhooked the captain's tag from his neck. Dalla, Esther, Harel witnessed; Besren called the ring closed. Zura's intent was to spare him — keep him alive as a thread to his handler. Caldren did not die.

Lawful demand after the duel: 'Name the mouth that fed you.' Caldren confessed: LAGO RHIAN — Zura's father, the Hollow One she has sworn to end — came through this circuit eight winters ago, taught Mai's sword-line to three wardens (two died, Caldren the third). Six winters later Lago returned, looked unchanged, breath fogged on a hot day; asked whether the circuit could be broken from the inside, then told Caldren which stones to let crack and in what order. Said when the seventh cracked 'someone will come and you will know them.' Caldren expected a man. Gave Caldren a bone token — finger-joint, carved with a single mark — said it would reward him but didn't say by whom. Also said 'I knew Lona's mother before she was her mother' as a warning. Caldren surrendered the token willingly, saying he did not know what it did and would do what Lago asked again if asked. Zura took the bone from Caldren's belt-stitching. It was WARM in her palm in a specific way (the way Lago's hand was warm when she was four and feverish); the mark on it matched the mark on the offering-grade iron nails that seal the ward-stones; it fit her hand like a tool made for it. She pocketed it cold-faced — only Lona saw her eyes go wrong for half a breath. Dalla saw something but Zura didn't read what.

Council's morning deliberation after the duel. Caldren banished from Holtfen and the warden-circuit the length of the Ironlands — walked west to the old Ashfen road by Harel and two of Harel's men, left with one day of supplies and no iron, no horse. Return on pain of death. Lona offered the captain's tag by the council; she accepted on condition that EWA (the third cut warden, still tending stones in the north) be given her tag back and asked what she wants. Harel placed the tag around Lona's neck. Dalla witnessed. The joint Iron Vow closed on a strong hit of Fulfill Your Vow (progress 10 vs 8,3), +2 XP to Zura.

Morning after Caldren's banishment. Zura attempted to Forge a Bond with Holtfen — miss. Community grateful but doesn't know her yet. Then found Lona at morning muster and offered to ride north together to find Ewa.

beats.text: The banishment was done before the sun cleared the treeline. Harel walked Caldren west himself — two wardens flanking, one day's bread, no iron — and the gate closed behind them without ceremony.
Lona wore the captain's tag for the first time at morning muster. The wardens decided, one by one, to let themselves believe in her.
Forge a Bond with Holtfen — miss (Heart 1+5 vs 8,9). The community is grateful but doesn't know her yet. Dismissed warmly as a traveler who did good work.
Zura crossed the yard to stand near Lona at muster — present, not requiring anything. Not interrupting.

beats.speaker: Lona
beats.text: You're still here. Most people who do what you did ride out the next morning. Caldren did. Every time.

beats.speaker: Lona
beats.text: I have to ride north today. Find Ewa. You could come.

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: I'll join you. We can both agree you'll need me to keep you safe.

beats.speaker: Lona
beats.text: I kept myself safe for three years cutting Caldren's circuit behind his back with no tag and no sanction. But yes. Fine. You can come and keep me safe.

text: Lona walked openly to the stone and returned Ewa's tag. Zura asked Ossian directly about the warm nail. Lona named the deserters Bren and Ossian and explained Hadris's forgiveness. Ossian confirmed the nail was warm when he held it. Deserters vow ticked to 32/40.

beats.text: Lona, Zura, and Grey walked openly to the stone. Lona held out Ewa's tag. 'Yours. The council gave it back. I asked them to.'

beats.speaker: Ewa
beats.text: You have the captain's tag. Caldren?

beats.speaker: Lona
beats.text: Banished. This is Zura Rhian — she's the reason.
Ewa took the tag. Bren's hand dropped from his belt. Ossian sat back down slowly.

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: Ossian. Where did you get the nail you put in Hadris?

beats.speaker: Ossian
beats.text: Caldren gave it to me. Said it was a sealing nail pulled from the northeast stone. Said to use it to discourage wardens who refused. I don't know if that's true about where it came from.

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: Why?

beats.speaker: Ossian
beats.text: Because when I held it, it was warm. Pulled nails aren't warm. Stone iron goes cold when it comes out. This one wasn't. You know what it means. That's why you're asking.
Tick progress: Ensure the deserters are no danger to Holtfen +2 marks (32/40). Finding them tending stones and walking willingly to council is the bulk of this vow.

metadata.track: Ensure the deserters are no danger to Holtfen

text: Mid-morning, the Hinge stone — the oldest stone on Holtfen's circuit, on Ewa's section of the eastern edge, set flush against the base of a split oak. Zura, Eddar, and Ewa walk out together; Lona stays in Holtfen. Ewa explains: most stones are set by wardens, replaced and recarved by each captain. The Hinge is different — no warden claims its setting, it's in the records as far back as records go, always in the same spot, always with the same mark. Every captain is told to leave it alone. Zura shows Eddar the mark on the stone's face — identical to the bone token. Eddar circles the stone, then crouches and reads the carving angle from the carver's working level. He concludes the stone was marked first, then the ward-line was drawn to include it. The Hinge isn't part of the circuit — the circuit was built around it. Forty years minimum. Whoever cut the mark intended the circuit to pass through it. Zura's father found this; he did not make it. Eddar asks Ewa if the stone has ever been warm; she recalls two winters ago, the hard one — three stones cracked in frost-heave, but the Hinge didn't. Snow melted around its base for a hand's width. She thought it was root-rot keeping the soil warm. Eddar concludes: it's been fed for decades — a permanent receiver, not a ward. He says he needs to know what's under the stone.

beats.speaker: Ewa
beats.text: The Hinge is the oldest stone on the circuit. Older than Sefa. Older than whoever Sefa learned from. It's the one we're told never needs tending — it holds itself.

beats.speaker: Ewa
beats.text: Most stones are set by wardens. Replaced, moved, recarved when the iron gets thin. My grandmother tended six stones that don't exist anymore. Lona's first posting was a stone Caldren moved two seasons later. The Hinge is different. No one placed it. It's in the records as far back as the records go, always in the same spot, always with the same mark.

A stone, waist-high, set flush against the base of a split oak. Dark iron driven deep into its crown — not a nail, a plate. On its face, cut deep enough that moss hasn't filled it in a generation: the mark. The same mark as the bone token in Zura's pack.

Eddar walks a slow circle around the stone, stave held across his body like a bar keeping him at distance. Then he crouches — not touching, just looking at the mark from the level where the carver would have worked.

beats.speaker: Eddar
beats.text: Inside face. This was carved before the circuit was sealed around it. The stone was marked first, then the ward-line was drawn to include it. Forty years. At least. Whoever cut this mark intended for the circuit to pass through it — not the other way around. The Hinge isn't part of the circuit. The circuit was built around the Hinge. Your father didn't make this. Your father found it.

beats.speaker: Eddar
beats.text: Has this stone ever been warm?

beats.speaker: Ewa
beats.text: I don't touch it. No one does. That's the rule. But two winters ago — the hard one — three stones cracked. The Hinge didn't. And when I passed it... the snow was melted around its base. A hand's width. I thought the oak roots were doing something. Rot beneath, maybe, keeping the soil warm.

beats.speaker: Eddar
beats.text: It's fed. It's been fed for decades. Not by a warden — by whoever made it. The iron plate isn't a ward. It's a receiver. Like the nail in Hadris, but permanent. Patient. I need to know what's under this stone.

text: Back at the Hinge. Eddar on his feet, stave raised. Ewa pressed against the oak. The overturned stone cracked clean in two; iron plate sheared. The bone disc in the cavity is dark now, cold — whatever was feeding it has stopped. Standing at the treeline opposite: an old woman, white-haired, weathered brown, in layered travel-worn leather. Staff taller than she is, iron-shod at both ends. Not threatening. Just watching. She says the anchor was already dying; she just made it quick. She introduces herself as Tavan — a Ledgerkeeper for this region before Lago was born, pushed out forty years ago after finding something in the records she wasn't meant to find. She reads Zura's iron — three nails that aren't hers and a bone older than Zura's grandmother — and recognizes Mai's sword-line in Zura's footwork. Tavan trained Mai forty years ago, not in the sword (Mai already had the sword-line from somewhere else) but in ledger-work. Mai left her thirty years ago to follow something north. Tavan has been walking the southern Hinterlands and the Deep Wilds edges since, mapping the old anchors. Six days ago the anchors started dying, south-to-north. Tavan has been following the failures north. The Hinge was the next one in the line. Zura tells Tavan that Mai found her after Greyhollow fell. Tavan realizes: Mai wasn't looking for Greyhollow — she was watching it. Zura asks what the real risk is of ignoring a failing network. Tavan: six anchors dead in six days, south to north — not collapse, a line being drawn in, consolidated. Spread across twenty anchors, now potentially in one place. Zura declares she's heading south to track the maintainers. Tavan: same direction, different reasons. Eddar will stay at the Hinge with Ewa. He warns Zura that Hollow Ones don't run — they circle. Zura sharp-questions: what makes a Hollow One run? Eddar admits it: Lago doesn't behave like a Hollow One. Something is keeping him alive and functional. A servant, not a component. Ewa says it.

beats.text: Eddar on his feet, stave raised. Ewa behind him, pressed against the oak. The overturned stone cracked clean in two — split down the middle, the iron plate sheared with it. The bone disc in the cavity is dark now. Cold. At the treeline opposite: an old woman. White-haired, weathered brown, layered travel-worn leather. A staff in one hand, taller than she is, iron-shod at both ends. She's not moving. Not threatening. Just there.

beats.speaker: Tavan
beats.text: It was already dying. I just made it quick.

beats.speaker: Tavan
beats.text: You carry three nails that aren't yours and a bone that's older than your grandmother. You move like someone trained by a sword-line I haven't seen in twenty years. My name is Tavan. I was a Ledgerkeeper for this region before your father was born. I left because I found something in the records I wasn't meant to find — and then someone made sure I couldn't stay. I'd like to know who taught you Mai's forms.

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: How do you know Mai?

beats.speaker: Tavan
beats.text: I trained her. Forty years ago, before she left the Hinterlands. She was my apprentice. Not in the sword — I don't fight. In the ledger-work. Reading iron, reading circuits, reading what's been done and by whom. The sword-line she carries came from somewhere else — she already had it when she came to me. Mai left me thirty years ago to follow something north. Wouldn't say what. I haven't seen her since.

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: I don't know what Mai was looking for. She left me without a word, but if it helps she found me after Greyhollow... fell.

beats.speaker: Tavan
beats.text: Mai went north thirty years ago. Greyhollow fell — twelve, thirteen years past? She spent nearly twenty years up there before it happened. And then she found you. A child. She wasn't looking for Greyhollow. She was watching it.

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: What does it matter if the anchors are failing and what they are feeding is dying? We are better off with nothing that needs feeding. The Understanding is enough to deal with.

beats.speaker: Tavan
beats.text: Maybe you're right. If the anchors die and whatever they fed starves — good. But things that are fed don't starve quietly. They look for other sources. And things that retreat don't always retreat because they're dying — sometimes they're consolidating. Six anchors dead in six days. All south to north. That's not collapse — that's a line being drawn in. If I'm right, whatever was spread across twenty anchors is now in one place.

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: What makes him run? I never heard of a Hollow One with an unfulfilled vow running.

beats.speaker: Eddar
beats.text: They don't run. They can't. The unfulfilled vow pulls them in circles — back to the site, back to the debt. Lago isn't stuck. Lago moves with purpose. He travels, he teaches, he plans. Something is fulfilling the vow for him. Holding the debt open without letting it collapse him. Feeding him, the way this network feeds the anchors. Which means whoever built this needed the Ironbinder alive and functional afterward.

beats.speaker: Ewa
beats.text: That's not a component. That's a servant.
Zura decides to go south alone. Tavan walks with her, same direction, different reasons. Eddar and Ewa remain at the Hinge to study the dead disc.

text: Session 11 — First Delve into the Anchor Network (Ancient/Underkeep, extreme rank). Zura, Tavan, and Grey entered via charged staff at the Tanglewood dead-trail-end. Segment 1 (shadow): miss — iron grate added from inside, cleared with Face Danger strong hit. Segment 2 (edge): weak hit — harrowing revelation: the Elvish wall-annotations are a log, Greyhollow was the first planned step. Segment 3 (wits): weak hit — junction chamber with a drained ward-stone slab, hostile Eld registered Zura's harvest vow in the network disc. Failed doubled-back ambush (miss, vow-burden: harvest debt makes her visible to the network). Segment 4 (edge): miss — noise delay, working sounds stopped ahead. Gathered Information strong hit with Grey: one person, alone, not fled. Entered the lit chamber. Found Mirin — young woman sent by Lago to feed ward-stone binding material into the live junction disc. Key revelations: (1) the network is Elvish infrastructure, not human-built; (2) Lago's plan is to re-seal the Waking Darkness from the ward-stones back into the deeper network; (3) the Eld have been tending the disc, improving integration — Tavan suspects the network is a VESSEL not a seal, monitoring how full it's getting; (4) Mai gave her staff to Mirin to bring it in, left it as a message for Zura; (5) Lago may have deliberately arranged Zura finding Mirin; (6) Mirin's contact is 4 days overdue, rations nearly spent. SESSION CONTINUATION: Gather Information weak hit (Tavan reads Mai's pattern via staff) — Mai went toward the network's center, leading Lago's debt-pull, not trailing it. She knew he'd be there. Zura swore Iron Vow to find Mai before she reaches Lago (strong hit after burning momentum, +2 momentum). Mirin joined group unarmed under threat. Segment 5 (edge, carved passages): miss — Reveal Danger: discovery complicates quest. At a junction, a second pattern joined Mai's trail from the left — someone met her deliberately. Mirin revealed: Lago's companion uses the left passage, has old iron-marks on her wrists, instructed Mirin to wait for someone carrying Greyhollow's iron. Also revealed: at least one other worker deeper in (south junction); the network has a threshold (center well); Mirin should have been extracted before the sequence completed — 4 days overdue. Segment 6 (edge, stairs into the depths): miss with match — staff loses navigation at depth, can no longer read Mai's pattern or trail. Two voices below, close. Companion calls up: 'She said you'd come down the stairs fast.' Gather Information weak hit (listening with Grey's Sharp): Mai's voice confirmed below, calm, mid-conversation. They were expected. Session ends: Zura one flight above Lago's companion on the staircase, Mai further below, arranged. Retroactive milestones applied: 3 on End What My Father Has Become (3/40 ticks); 1 on Find Mai Before She Reaches Lago (8/40 ticks).

beats.text: Entry into the Anchor Network. Tavan presses the iron-shod base of her staff against the bare earth at the dead trail end. The anchor-marks along the shaft fill with something that is not light. The ground does not open — it unhides. A passage has always been here. Stone steps, worn smooth, leading down into warm air that smells of iron and old growth. Grey refuses to go first.

Delve the Depths +Shadow 2. Action 5 vs 7, 7 — miss with match. Reveal a Danger: 'Your way is blocked or trapped.' The match means this is structurally significant — not an accident but a deliberate countermeasure set from inside.

Zura chooses to work the bar through the gap — staff tip or sword tip — rather than use the mechanism (which would broadcast their presence) or break the hinge (which would be loud). Quiet, physical, no charge spent.
Face Danger +Edge 2 to work the bar through the gap with a blade or staff tip. Action 3+2=5 vs 3, 1 — strong hit. Bar lifted clean. +1 momentum (now 5).

Gather Information +Wits 1 +1 (Hound Sharp) = +2. Action 4+2=6 vs 6, 4 — weak hit. No one waiting immediately ahead; passage clear. But Grey kept returning to sniff the air upward at one spot — something above registers their presence. The network's live iron read them on entry. +1 momentum (now 6).

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: "There is nothing but to proceed." Nods at Grey to lead. Sword drawn, torch held aloft.

Delve the Depths +Edge 2. Action 1+2=3 vs 2, 6 — weak hit. Subtable d100 = 10 (Edge 1-45): Mark progress AND Reveal a Danger. Site: 2/40 ticks, 1 segment. Danger rolled 78 (main table): 'You confront a harrowing situation or sensation.'

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: "These tunnels, they are older than that plan. Someone is using the power of this place to carry out their plan, scribbling over the older writing?"

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: "Is this... elvish?"

Zura follows Grey deeper. Uncertain of purpose, but unable to turn back. The revelation about Greyhollow being the first step in the plan is carried forward, not resolved. The old Elvish writing recedes behind them.

Delve the Depths +Wits 1. Action 4+1=5 vs 9, 1 — weak hit. Subtable d100 = 39 (Wits 1-40): Mark progress AND Reveal a Danger. Site: 4/40 ticks, 2 segments. Danger rolled 54 (main table): 'You encounter a hostile denizen.'

Standoff in the junction chamber. Zura holds still, sword ready but lowered, studying the Eld for intent. Grey remains between them. The Eld circles the junction disc slowly, keeping distance, the iron-wire coil on its forearm warming. Then it raises the weighted cord and the iron weight begins to circle without wrist movement — taking measure of Zura's vow-debt directly.

Secure an Advantage +Wits 1 to read the Eld's movement. Action 3+1=4 vs 5, 2 — weak hit. Burn offered (momentum 6 vs dice 5, 2), declined. +1 momentum (now 7). Advantage short-lived — reads the Eld's lateral preference, cord arm, and split attention on the junction disc.
Zura holds. Gestures Grey to stand by. Watches the Eld at the junction disc rather than acting.

Face Danger +Shadow 2. Lead into left passage then double back to shadow the junction. Action 2+2=4 vs 10, 7 — miss. Pay the Price: harvest vow resonates with the freshly-written junction disc; ambush position exposed to the network. -1 momentum (now 6). Complication theme: vow-burden.

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: "Stealth will not help us here. There was nothing we can do without going to war against that Eld and his entire kind in these tunnels. Let's keep moving to find those we are looking for."

Delve the Depths +Edge 2. Action 4+2=6 vs 10, 7 — miss. No progress. Reveal a Danger: 'You lose your way or are delayed.' Moving fast toward the light and working sounds — hit an unseen junction, Grey splits left, Zura right. Brief separation; regroup costs time. The working sounds stop the moment they make noise. The person ahead has been warned. -1 momentum (now 5).
Zura chooses slow approach — no stealth (the network sees her regardless), but deliberate. Using Grey's sense of smell to read what is ahead before committing.

Gather Information +Wits 1 +1 (Hound Sharp) = +2. Action 5+2=7 vs 2, 3 — strong hit. Grey reads ahead: one person, alone, not fled — waiting and listening. Scent matches the leather strap fragment from the surface (confirmed quarry). Not combat stance — working posture, interrupted mid-task. Live iron and stone dust in the air. +3 momentum total (now 8).

Zura enters the lit chamber — sword sheathed, hands ready. Finds: a young woman alone, kneeling beside a fully-live junction disc (the source of the blue-white light), tools at her feet, a fragment of ward-stone material in one hand. Days underground. Not frightened. Tired. She looks up at Zura and speaks first.

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: "Who are you?"
Zura positions Grey at the dark passage, settles in front of Mirin with exits in sight and sword reach. Tactical control established. Then asks directly about the work.

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: "The people." / "What are you doing, Mirin? Are you breaking the stones or strengthening the seals? Does your work need Greyhollow and Ashfen... and Holtfen to die to succeed?"

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: "I think you're just a useful idiot. You don't know what was released when the stone broke. Are you alone in these tunnels? What are you supposed to do next after you are done here?" Spoken slowly, calmly, as if bored. Never acknowledges Lago's name.

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: "What have you done with Mai? We found her staff." Deflects Mirin's question entirely. The implied threat of violence is real and close to the surface — a throat's width away from being stated.

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: "You said those who were going to come here are overdue. How many times were you visited by them? How many come? What are you supposed to do if they don't come?"

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: "Have the Eld come to you?"

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: "Then the question is why Mirin and her friends are tampering with the discs in the first place. To who's benefit are they re-aligning the Understanding to?"

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: "Do you or any of your people know how to use the discs, the Understanding web in these tunnels? Does he know?"

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: "I wonder why he hasn't come for you yet." Pause. "What were you feeding it and do you know how to reverse it?"

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: "Tavan, do you think you might be able to control the power in these stones/discs?"

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: "Can you read the network to find the other... to find him? The way the network can find me."

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: "And Mai, can you find her?"
Zura tells Tavan: "Find Mai. We find out what she knows and what her objectives are here." Tavan uses the staff to read the network for Mai's pattern.

Gather Information +Wits (1). Action die 6, score 7 vs 4, 9 — weak hit. +1 momentum (8→9). Tavan reads Mai's pattern: she came through this junction ~1 week ago and went deeper toward the network's center. The complication: her direction maps to the same vector as Lago's debt-signature — she went toward him, not away.

beats.speaker: Tavan
beats.text: "She went toward him. The debt-pull your father carries in this network — the weight of Greyhollow, the Ironbinder's oath he broke — it has a direction. A draw. Everything in the network bends toward where that unresolved iron sits heaviest. Mai's pattern doesn't trail it. It leads it. She got there before him, or she's moving to meet him. Either way, she went toward the heaviest part of this iron. She knew he would be there."
Zura: "We need to find her, before she gets to him. We can't deal with them both together." Party moves to push deeper into the network following Mai's pattern. Mirin situation pending.

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: "You can come with us. You will bring no tools or weapons. If we encounter any of your people, you better stay very clear or you will be the first I will kill." Calm.
Zura draws her blade and runs her palm along the edge. Quiet oath-swearing — blood on iron — before entering the carved passage. No witness but Tavan, Grey, and Mirin at the tunnel mouth.
Swear an Iron Vow +Heart (1). Action die 4, score 5 vs 2, 5 — weak hit. Burned momentum (9 → 2) for strong hit. +2 momentum (→ 4). Vow created: Find Mai Before She Reaches Lago, dangerous rank.

Delve the Depths +Edge (2). Action die 1, score 3 vs 8, 9 — miss. Reveal a Danger (rolled 74 → main table): a discovery undermines or complicates your quest. At a junction, Tavan reads a second pattern joined Mai's trail — someone met her here and continued with her. Grey recognises the scent and is troubled. Mirin recognises the left passage.

At the junction: two trails go forward. Mai's pattern (via staff) plus a second unknown pattern that joined her from the left passage. The patterns show meeting, not struggle. Grey recognises the unknown scent with unease. Mirin presses against the wall, staring at the left passage — she recognises something about it.

beats.speaker: Mirin
beats.text: "He travels with someone. She comes through the network separately — not always with him, sometimes ahead of him. I've only seen her once. She came to check my progress about three weeks ago. She didn't give a name. She looked at my work, told me I was feeding the sequence correctly, and left. She gave me one instruction: if you see someone come through carrying Greyhollow's iron — dead colony, unresolved debt — don't approach them, don't speak first. Wait. Let them come to you."

Grey places the scent from the left passage: the camp south of the march-track, weeks ago — Lago and one unknown companion. The companion who anticipated Zura is now ahead with Mai. Tavan goes very still at the revelation.

beats.speaker: Mirin
beats.text: "There's at least one other worker. Deeper in, south junction. Different section — we weren't meant to meet. The companion: calm in a bad way. Not young. Old iron-marks on her wrists, very old. Carried something under her wrap that wasn't a disc-tool. I was given a timeline — I was supposed to leave before the center well reaches threshold. The contact who was supposed to extract me is four days late. I don't know if the sequence has already completed."

The vessel theory confirmed: the network has a threshold. Workers were instructed to evacuate before it's reached. Mirin may already be past the safe window. Tavan reacts with quiet confirmation rather than surprise — she suspected this. At least one other worker is deeper in the network. The companion has old iron-marks on her wrists.
Zura: "We need to keep moving." Party pushes forward from the junction, following the merged trail of Mai and the companion toward the center well.

Delve the Depths +Edge (2). Action die 3, score 5 vs 10, 10 — miss with match. Reveal a Danger (rolled 86 → main): a resource is diminished, broken, or lost. The staff's anchor-marks go dark at depth — can no longer read Mai's pattern or navigate the network below this point. Match: voices below, two of them, close. They may have been heard coming down the stairs.

The staff's trail-reading fails mid-staircase — the deep network uses older iron the upper marks cannot parse. Trail to Mai is lost. Match consequence: two voices audible below, very close. The haste on the stairs may have announced their arrival. Mirin alerts Zura silently.

Gather Information +Wits (1) +1 (Grey Sharp). Action die 4, score 6 vs 1, 9 — weak hit. +1 momentum (move) +1 momentum (Sharp on hit) = +2 total (→ 6). Heard: measured footsteps coming up one flight, then stopping. The companion's voice — calm, older, expected them. 'She said you'd come down the stairs fast.' Second voice below is Mai's, in conversation, not distressed.

beats.speaker: Lago's companion
beats.text: "You can douse the torch if you want. Or keep it. It makes no difference to us. She said you'd come down the stairs fast."

text: Session 12 — Heart of the Anchor Network. Zura descended to meet Serin on the staircase landing: Lago's companion, iron-marks on her wrists, fourteen years in the network. Entered the chamber to find Mai and Lago mid-argument over the sealing method. First words: "Mai." Then: "Father." Lago's hollow face, the shape of warmth without the warmth. Zura revealed she carries Ashfen's debt in addition to Greyhollow's. Lago admitted he knew the circuit was failing but hadn't planned for her taking Ashfen's burden. Zura swore Iron Vow in blood to Complete the Harvest Debt — Seal at Greyhollow (miss with match, -2 momentum, pressed on). Lago stepped forward to refuse; Zura silenced him — "You made your choices without me." He stepped aside: "You have your mother's certainty." Gave her his iron piece to navigate. Fulfill Your Vow: Find Mai — strong hit with match, +2 XP. Lago confessed the Eld have been sustaining him through the network for fourteen years; their goal is the darkness contained within Elvish infrastructure. The disc quickened when Zura swore — the Eld heard the oath. Footsteps above. Group splits: Zura+Grey+Tavan west into dark ancient passages, Mai+Lago south to the threshold, Serin+Mirin east as a draw. Session ends with Zura heading west, sword sheathed, Tavan's staff humming behind her.

beats.text: Descent to the staircase landing. Torch light on old stone. Serin waiting with her back to the wall, arms loose, iron-marks catching the light. She doesn't move at the drawn blade.

beats.speaker: Serin
beats.text: She said you'd be carrying the dog and the old woman's staff. She was right on both counts.

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: You seem to know a lot. Who are you?

beats.speaker: Serin
beats.text: Serin. Fourteen years in this network. I work with Lago — not for him. That distinction matters. Mai is below. She's safe — for the moment. Whether that stays true depends on what happens in the next hour.

Serin explains: Lago wants to re-seal the Waking Darkness permanently into the network. Mai has been arguing against it for six hours. The method is the disagreement — Lago's plan turns the network into a vessel, leaking into the junctions over decades. Serin and Mai believe there is a cleaner solution.
Zura proposes taking the conversation to Mai and Lago directly. Serin agrees. The group descends.

The chamber: round, high-ceilinged, walls dense with Elvish inscription-lines layered over centuries. A junction disc four paces across, alive and pulsing slow as breath. Two figures: Mai — older, white at temples, same economy of movement. Lago — her father's frame, the warmth gone, hollow eyes, the look of a fire burned down long ago.

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: Mai. ...Father.
Lago says her name. Quiet, older than she remembers. The hollow thing receiving something it wasn't expecting. Mai watches with an expression complicated and controlled.

beats.speaker: Mai
beats.text: I wondered which of you she'd look at first.
Zura waits. The argument between Mai and Lago resumes. The core: distributed containment in the network vs a clean solution. Mai says: 'And she just walked in.' Both look at Zura.

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: If I'm the solution, I should know how that is the case.

beats.speaker: Mai
beats.text: The Waking Darkness came through Greyhollow — that's where the seal failed. The real binding was the living vow-debt of the colony itself. The colony is dead. But its harvest vow isn't. You carry it.

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: I also carry Ashfen now.

Mai recalculates. Asks when. Lago admits he knew the circuit was decaying, didn't plan for Zura taking Ashfen's debt specifically. Two colony debts combined: stronger seal but considerably more weight for the person standing at the origin site.

beats.speaker: Lago
beats.text: I had planned to do it myself. Serin told me it would destroy what is left of me. I had decided that was acceptable. But the debt isn't mine to close. I cannot ask you to do this.

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: I never asked you to break your oath. You still carry it as whatever you've become — but I also carry you. I carry your sin everywhere I go, and here I am. I am here to end it.
Zura lowers her blade, realizing she had been pointing it at him.

Swear an Iron Vow — Complete the Harvest Debt, Seal at Greyhollow (Heart 1 + adds 1 vs 8, 8). Miss with match. The disc quickens — the network and the Eld hear the oath. Lago steps forward to refuse. Pressed on: -2 momentum (now 4).

beats.speaker: Zura
beats.text: It is not for you to decide. You made your choices a long time ago without me and now I do not need you to approve. I made my vow with blood on iron.
Lago steps aside. 'You have your mother's certainty.' He gives Zura an iron piece scored with the anchor-mark to navigate west.

beats.speaker: Mai
beats.text: The path to Greyhollow is closed from the surface. The site has been consumed. The only way in is through the network. Together, or not at all.
Fulfill Your Vow — Find Mai Before She Reaches Lago. Progress score 4 vs 2, 2. Strong hit with match. Vow fulfilled: Zura found Mai at the only moment that mattered. +2 XP (total 4).

beats.speaker: Lago
beats.text: The network has been keeping me functional. The Eld built this. They maintain it. They have been allowing me to use it because my work served them. I believed I was using their infrastructure for my purpose. I think I have been their instrument for fourteen years.

beats.speaker: Tavan
beats.text: The disc quickened when you swore the vow. That wasn't the oath landing in the iron. They heard it. They know.
Footsteps above — measured, unhurried. The Eld moving through the upper passages toward the chamber.
Zura calls the split: she and Grey and Tavan take the west passage (dark, ancient, untended by Eld). Mai and Lago south to the threshold. Serin and Mirin east as a draw.
Session ends: Zura sheathes her sword and heads west. The west passage swallows torchlight quickly. Tavan's staff hums behind her. Grey moves ahead into the dark.
